verdict.rationale: Turso's docs claim it is "Fully backwards compatible with SQLite" and that local databases are "fully SQLite-compatible — they open existing SQLite files". libSQL is described as a fork of SQLite. Hands-on community reports concretely contradict the "fully" claim: one says savepoints, window functions and ATTACH DATABASE are missing, another says PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL cross-process reads fail with an exclusive lock, and a third says file-format compatibility breaks once Turso extensions are used. Missing for 10: verified parity with SQLite features (savepoints, window functions, ATTACH, WAL multi-process behavior), documentation of SQLite extension loading, and independent confirmation that existing SQLite code runs unmodified.

support.subject: As a developer, I get real engine compatibility — the Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite dialect and extensions my existing code expects — not a lookalike subset

citations.quote: Fully backwards compatible with SQLite, but built for the next generation
They are fully SQLite-compatible — they open existing SQLite files — and run entirely in your process, no server needed
libSQL is an open source, open contribution fork of SQLite, created and maintained by Turso.
